compositionTool: python3 + Pillow 12.2.0 (crop / paste / LANCZOS resize); labels in Arial Bold + Arial. No ImageMagick, no browser rendering. Full-page primaries are byte copies, never scaled.
howToRead: Read @16 and dE76>10 (dE76AboveVisibleRatio), never @1 on its own - @1 counts any 1/255 change and is dominated by sub-perceptual noise, which is why /pricing @1 falls 0.3914 -> 0.0266 while the amplitude-gated @16 falls only 0.0295 -> 0.0158. In every route family, SOURCE is the live page, OLD is the pre-28.5B reconstruction, HARDENED is the post-28.5B reconstruction, and a DIFF paints changed pixels red against a washed-out copy of the page, so a smaller and fainter red field is better. Both diffs in a family are measured against the identical live-original bytes, so old-vs-new is a fair comparison; the old build was generated from a five-day-older source, which disadvantages it, so every improvement shown is a lower bound. Images 19-22 and diagnostics 02 and 03 are the exception to all of the above: they document a KNOWN UNFIXED responsive defect that 28.5B did not address and that is carried forward to 28.5C - do not read them as evidence of an improvement.

conventions.changedRatioAt1: fraction of overlapping pixels where ANY channel differs by >=1/255. Noise-dominated; never the verdict on its own.
conventions.changedRatioAt16: fraction of overlapping pixels where the max channel delta is >=16/255. Amplitude-gated; this is the primary visible-regression channel.
conventions.dE76AboveJndRatio: fraction of overlapping pixels with CIE dE76 > 2.3, the just-noticeable difference. THIS is the field reported as 'dE76' in the 28.5B verdict tables.
conventions.dE76AboveVisibleRatio: fraction of overlapping pixels with CIE dE76 > 10, i.e. clearly different side by side. Read this together with @16.
conventions.dE76Mean: mean CIE dE76 over the overlapping area.
conventions.heightDelta: clone full-page height minus source full-page height, in CSS pixels. 0 is exact parity.
conventions.commonAreaRatio: fraction of the union area that both images actually cover. Below 1 means the two pages are different sizes and part of the comparison is undefined.
conventions.diffRendering: red pixels = changed pixels, drawn over a lightened copy of the source. Bigger and denser red = worse.
conventions.nullMetrics: null means the channel is not applicable to that image (a source or clone capture is not itself a measurement) or was not recorded by that QA run - it never means zero.

comparability: SAME_REFERENCE_COMPARABLE between old and new diffs; old clone built from 2026-08-25 source (drift caveat)
comparabilityDetail: SAME_REFERENCE_COMPARABLE between old and new diffs: both sides are diffed against the IDENTICAL live-original PNG bytes captured in the 2026-08-30T15-57-54-926Z QA session, so the reference is held fixed and old-vs-new channel deltas are attributable to the clone. CAVEAT: the old clone was generated from the 2026-08-25 observation/site-spec source, five days older than the reference capture, so any real linear.app drift in that window is charged to the old clone. The comparison therefore DISADVANTAGES the old build; improvements it shows are a lower bound, and any place where the old build wins is not explainable by drift.

verdictNumbersSummary.note: old -> new, both diffed against the identical live-original capture. Arrays are [old, new].

secondSite.note: stripe.com, a DIFFERENT site and a different QA run (2026-08-30T16-17-33-405Z). No old-build counterpart exists, so these are absolute fidelity numbers, not improvements. Only @16 and heightDelta are recorded by that run.

knownUnfixed: Responsive variant coverage: only 390px and 1440px viewports were observed, so every width in between renders one of those two variants. At 914px the clone still serves the 390px column (diagnostic-03, heightDelta +724, commonAreaRatio 0.9061).

The /pricing comparison table appears in the clone only at >=1232px while the live source shows it by 1100px, losing the header row, three of four value columns and 286 characters of visible text inside that band (images 21-22, diagnostic-02).
stripe.com/industries/media-entertainment on MOBILE is the corpus outlier at @16 0.1976 / heightDelta +924 (diagnostic-04), driven by horizontal box metrics rather than missing content.
/changelog is +1px taller than the live source in BOTH the old and the hardened build - pre-existing, unchanged by 28.5B.
